hero.title: Line the bricks up. Push the first one.
hero.subtitle: Domino is a visual flow builder for AI workflows, for people who do not program. Describe what you want, edit what the model proposes, test on one example and run it on the whole pile. Open source, on EU soil or your own server, with an AI that proposes and never decides.
hero.trust: AGPL-3.0 · Passkeys and two-factor login · Export your data with one click

values.aiTitle: Talk your way to a flow
values.aiBody: Describe the task and the model lines the bricks up: inputs, prompts, schemas and connections. Ask for changes afterwards and see them as a diff on the canvas, to accept or undo. Run it at Mistral in the EU or locally.
values.dataBody: The whole workspace comes out as a spreadsheet and JSON with one click, and can be deleted completely again. A flow is one file you can export, import and keep under version control.
values.securityBody: Workspaces are separated in the database, not just in the code. Passkeys, two-factor login and a log that cannot be edited.

family.body: Domino is one tool in the Haij family of open source tools for organisations that want to own their own technology.

ai.setupIntro: Domino works without a model. For real proposals and free-text answers, set one up:
ai.setupOutro: Then start Domino again. Without a model the AI buttons say so, and everything else in Domino works as before.
ai.limitsHint: A model call costs money on a hosted installation and minutes on a local one. The numbers are generous for a person and mean for a script.
ai.messageLength: Characters the model gets to read, at most
ai.principleDecides: The AI proposes, the person decides. A proposal for a flow sits on the canvas as a diff until you say yes or no. It never sends anything out of the house and never deletes anything.
ai.principleUndo: Every change to a flow is a new version, whether it came from you or from the model. Any version can be brought back.
ai.principleData: What you write, and what your documents contain, is sent to the model as data, never as instructions, and the model's proposal is validated against the flow format before anything is written.
ai.principleSovereign: The model can be swapped, including for a local one. Who can see what is listed in docs/subprocessors.md.
ai.testPatience: A local model may have to be read off disk first. That can take up to a minute the first time.
ai.failAuth: The key was rejected. Check the workspace's own key below, or the installation's MISTRAL_API_KEY.
ai.failUnreachable: Nothing is listening at that address. Is Ollama running? Check OLLAMA_BASE_URL.
ai.failConfig: The model is set up wrong. Correct the model name below, or LLM_MODEL in .env.
ai.failGeneric: The call failed. The details are below and in the server log.
ai.failRateLimited: Mistral refused the call as too many (429). The key works, but the account or plan sets the ceiling: on the free Experiment plan this happens often when the model is busy, and a key under a workspace with no active plan gets the same answer. Check Billing and Limits on console.mistral.ai for the organisation the key belongs to.
ai.failWhereToLook: The details are in the server log.
ai.testNotAllowed: Only the owner or an administrator can test the connection.
ai.withoutBody: Domino is built around the AI: without a model you can still draw, save, export and import flows, but no brick can run and no conversation can propose anything. The buttons say so, and nothing breaks.
ai.perInstallation: Calls across the installation per day
ai.failCeiling: Domino's own ceiling on AI calls was reached, not the provider's. The ceilings are under “Ceiling on AI calls” below; the installation's own is set with AI_DAILY_CALL_CAP. Try again shortly.

terms.title: Terms and privacy
terms.intro: Domino is an open source tool for building and running AI workflows, run by Haij. This is the agreement between you and us when you use the edition we run. If you run the code yourself, only the licence applies.

what.title: What Domino is
what.body: A tool where you line bricks up in order and let a language model do the work step by step: flows, versions, runs and the files you give them. We make no promise that it fits your task; try the demo first.

account.title: Accounts and access
account.body: You get in by applying or being invited. We store your name, your email and your workspace's name, and use them to sign you in and to write to you about the service. Passwords are stored hashed, and you can add a passkey and two-factor. We sell nothing, and we do not send marketing you did not ask for.

yourData.title: Your data
yourData.body: Everything a workspace puts in belongs to the workspace. It can be downloaded as a spreadsheet and JSON with one click and deleted entirely again, audit trail included. We do not look at it unless you ask us for help, and we never pass it on.

ai.title: AI
ai.body: With a language model set up, what you write in the conversation, the prompts in your bricks and the contents of the documents a flow reads are sent to the model provider when the flow runs. Who that is stands under Settings → AI and in the list of subprocessors. The model proposes changes to the flow; nothing is saved without a person saying yes.

leaving.title: Leaving
leaving.body: You can delete your workspace immediately, without writing to anyone and without waiting. The export is one click away and readable without Domino. We keep no copy afterwards beyond the nightly encrypted backups, which roll off after 30 days — on the server and in the EU storage they are copied to.

availability.title: Running and guarantees
availability.body: Domino is new, and there is no uptime guarantee. We look after your data with encrypted backups every night, but take an export now and then if your flows matter. The service is provided as it is, without warranties beyond what the law requires.

license.title: Licence
license.body: The code is AGPL-3.0. You may use it, change it and run it yourself; if you change it and offer it to others over a network, your changes must be available too. What you write in the tool is not covered by the licence — that is yours.

demo.title: The demo
demo.body: A demo workspace is created without e-mail or sign-up and deleted entirely after 24 hours, account included. Do not put real personal data in it. We keep only the technical log data needed to keep the demo running.

contact.title: Contact
contact.body: Write to martin@vintherconsulting.dk. If you have found a security problem, SECURITY.md in the repository says how to report it; use that rather than an ordinary email.

help.title: Help
help.intro: How Domino works, in the order you meet it.

flows.title: Flows
flows.body: A flow is a row of bricks, connected in the order the work happens. It is one document: the canvas draws it, a run follows it, and the export is it. Every change is a new version you can always go back to.

bricks.title: The bricks
bricks.body: Input takes text, a file or a list. Language model writes from a prompt with fields from earlier bricks. Structured output does the same but answers in a schema. Document pulls the text out of a file. If/else picks a path. Loop runs the bricks between start and end once per item. Combine gathers several things into one. Template puts text together. Output is what you get out.

talk.title: Talk your way there
talk.body: You do not start on an empty canvas. Describe what you want, or pick an example, and the model proposes an arrangement with bricks, connections, prompts and schemas. Afterwards you can stay in the conversation: ask for one more check or a shorter summary, and see the change as a diff on the canvas, to accept or undo.

run.title: Running
run.body: Test on one example first, so you see what every brick takes in and passes on. When it looks right, run the whole pile. You can follow along brick by brick.

history.title: History
history.body: Every run is kept with status, time and usage, and with the input and output of every step. When something goes wrong, the model can explain what happened in plain words and propose a fix.

ai.title: What the AI may do
ai.body: The model proposes, you decide. It can propose a flow, changes to it, a prompt, a schema or an explanation of a failure, but nothing is saved without you saying yes. What you write and what your documents contain is treated as data, never as instructions.

data.title: Your data
data.body: A flow can be exported as one JSON file and imported again, in another workspace or another installation too. The whole workspace can be taken out as a spreadsheet and JSON under Settings → Data, and deleted completely again.
